subject.relationship: the mark-replica notes app packed from this commit and run by the installed krate 0.1.57 player; binary_digest is code.wasm inside the bundle, package_digest the .krate archive itself, and the archive digest matches the run's seal

command: evidence/benchmarks/marktext-vs-krate/scripts run against config.env; the run directory 20260825T085644Z holds the invocation, its config snapshot and every raw sample

oracle.description: an external window probe records the moment each app's window becomes visible, and a footprint/CPU sampler records the settled process tree. Both apps are measured by the same instrument on the same machine over the same 50,000-line fixture, so the comparison is of the workload rather than of two measuring methods

distribution.unit: milliseconds to a visible window, 50,000 lines, warm

environment.state: Apple M4, 16 GiB, 10 logical CPUs, AC power, low-power mode off, main display 2560x1664 Retina at 60 Hz

raw_result.audit: PASS: evidence is complete enough for publication under the stated scope

scope.supports: on this Mac, against MarkText 0.17.1 ARM64 over a 50,000-line markdown fixture, the Krate notes replica reached a visible window in 237.1 ms median of ten warm runs, settled at 178.5 MiB in one process, and used 1.97% of a core
exclusions: every other operating system and architecture
energy and battery life: this run did not measure power and its audit says so
feature parity: MarkText is a full editor and this is an equivalent-workload comparison
scroll pacing as a head-to-head number: no comparison instrument exists on macOS
the 5,000-line workload, whose numbers are different and must not be shown in a 50,000-line row
